name: Microneedling (SkinPen)
lead: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, skin needling or dermarolling, is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin; SkinPen is a branded electric microneedling device used in registered clinical trials.[1] It has been used for scarring and acne, and is combined in some practices with platelet-rich plasma.[1]

Registered SkinPen trials cover wrinkles of the neck, acne scars on the face and back, acne vulgaris, hand aging and vitiligo.[3][4][5][6][7] No results from these registrations are summarised in the sources reviewed here.
The sources reviewed do not describe the device history or its regulatory clearance, although it is commonly described as FDA-cleared.
infobox: Wrinkles, acne scars, acne, hand aging, vitiligo

paras: Registered, completed studies of SkinPen include neck wrinkles (35 participants),[3] acne scars on the face or back (41),[4] facial acne vulgaris as a proof of concept (31),[5] hand aging (18),[6] and microneedling as a stand-alone vitiligo treatment (13).[7] A hand aging study was withdrawn,[8] and a study of microneedling for dermatoporosis is also registered.[2] Other registered work compares microneedling with fractional laser or with platelet-rich plasma.[9][10] Wikipedia states that some studies found adding microneedling to minoxidil more effective for hair loss than minoxidil alone, and that research on scars and acne is ongoing.[1]

Wikipedia notes infection concerns when procedures are performed by untrained people in non-medical settings, and describes an April 2024 CDC report of three women diagnosed with HIV after vampire facials at a New Mexico spa.[1]

card.summary: Branded electric microneedling pen with several small registered trials on scars, wrinkles and acne; published results were not located here.
card.note: Infection risk with unsterile or non-clinical use.

quick.overview:
SkinPen is an electric microneedling device that makes controlled tiny punctures in the skin, used by clinicians for acne scars and signs of aging.

Several small trials are registered for different skin conditions.
quick.mechanism: Repeated tiny punctures are thought to trigger skin repair and collagen production; this is the standard description of microneedling.
quick.risks: Infection is a documented risk in untrained or non-sterile settings, including a 2024 CDC report tied to a spa facial procedure.
